title: feat: request outcomes, traffic groups and a range picker on observability
author: ElliotEtag

gist.summary: The internal Platform & Usage dashboard now separates requests rejected for insufficient Pollen from requests that failed after the balance check. Over the last 30 days, 55% of regular calls were rejected before metering, almost all with HTTP 402; 8% failed after the balance check; and about 13,000 users had such a request. A new table ranks the top 30 models by failed funded requests, with respan/span-01-lite showing a 99.5% failure rate. Hourly load is now split by traffic group, exposing legacy bridges—about 54% of all calls—alongside operations and dev traffic. A 7/30/90-day picker stores the selection in `?range=` and passes it to Grafana as `from` and `to`; the unused legacy-folder filter was removed, and the dashboard title no longer shifts when switching views. Users & Balances now labels negative balances as 'Accounts in Quest debt' and 'Accounts in Paid overdraft' in a neutral colour because both states are allowed by design. D7 activation now has a rate line, recently at 52–63%. All panel queries were checked read-only at 7, 30 and 90 days. At 90 days, dashboards loaded in under 1.1 seconds except Users & Balances at about 10.6 seconds, due to its existing WAU query and within the 60-second timeout. No Tinybird changes were made.

image.prompt: In a cozy pixel art garden workspace, Polli studies three softly glowing dashboard charts on a CRT monitor, with lime green (#ecf874) bars, pastel traffic-group flowers, and a tiny 7/30/90 calendar beside them. The main character is a cute pixel art bee mascot with a yellow body and dark brown horizontal stripes, small black legs, two black antennae, black vertical oval eyes, bright pink rectangular blush marks on cheeks, a small happy smile, and small rounded light blue translucent wings; she wears tiny analyst glasses, stays small within the scene, and is strictly pixel art, never realistic. Cozy pixel art, 8-bit aesthetic, soft pastel gradients, warm lighting, retro gaming vibes.
